verdict_reasoning: No surviving objection is fatal, and no level fails. A committer who knows the not-null code reviewed the design, and the author followed him. The open points are fixable: the F492 remark (standards-compat-1), the SET NOT NULL error (standards-compat-2) and unproven dump round-trip for mixed hierarchies (prior-attempts-1). Demand (demand-1, demand-2) rests only on standard conformance, which lowers priority but does not block.

brief.title: Allow NOT ENFORCED on not-null constraints
brief.problem: Postgres supports NOT ENFORCED for foreign key and CHECK constraints but not for not-null constraints, so sql_features.txt lists F492 with the remark "except not-null constraints". The author wants to complete F492. The thread does not name users who asked for this or a use case beyond standard conformance.
brief.proposed_design: A NOT ENFORCED not-null constraint is stored in pg_constraint with conenforced and convalidated both false, and pg_attribute.attnotnull stays false, so nulls are accepted and existing rows are not checked. A column keeps at most one not-null constraint, and the rules forbid an enforced parent with a not-enforced child. A column that inherits conflicting statuses from several parents gets an enforced constraint.
user_visible_surface: SQL syntax: NOT NULL NOT ENFORCED in CREATE TABLE column and table constraints, and in ALTER TABLE ADD CONSTRAINT ... NOT NULL col NOT ENFORCED.
Catalog semantics: pg_attribute.attnotnull now means an enforced (possibly invalid) not-null constraint exists.
New errors: SET NOT NULL, VALIDATE CONSTRAINT and ALTER CONSTRAINT ... ENFORCED fail on a not-enforced not-null constraint.
pg_dump emits NOT NULL NOT ENFORCED inline in CREATE TABLE (v4 onward).
author_claims: The patch completes SQL feature F492 and removes the "except not-null constraints" remark.
The regression tests cover the inheritance, partitioning and MERGE/SPLIT PARTITIONS corner cases.
Changing a constraint's enforceability later is unsupported, so the complexity of commit 0cd17fdd3c does not apply yet.
brief.thread_state: Álvaro Herrera reviewed the design and the author changed multiple-inheritance handling, the hint, and pg_dump output to follow him; a separate CREATE TABLE LIKE bug fix was committed by Peter Eisentraut. Solai v reported v5 tests passing, and Sebas Mannem plans to test v6; psql tab completion, raised by Haritabh Gupta, has no visible answer.
unclear: The commit message does not explain the different rule for partitions, where an enforced parent seems to forbid not-enforced partitions only in v1 wording.
The thread does not say whether the planner or executor ever uses a not-enforced not-null constraint, for example in proving IS NOT NULL.
The commit message lists DROP NOT NULL removal twice and does not say how ALTER COLUMN DROP NOT NULL treats inherited not-enforced constraints.
The thread does not say how pg_upgrade and dumps from older servers handle the attnotnull meaning change.
No visible reply confirms that v6 fixed the 002_pg_dump.pl failures reported for v4.

prior_attempts.title: Revert "Improve compression and storage support with inheritance"
prior_attempts.quote: pg_dump cannot currently dump all the structures that are allowed by this patch.
prior_attempts.reason:
This reverts commit 0413a556990ba628a3de8a0b58be020fd9a14ed0.

pg_dump cannot currently dump all the structures that are allowed by
this patch.  This needs more work in pg_dump and more test coverage.
prior_attempts.what_is_different: P20 was about compression and storage inheritance, a different feature. Its reason applies because this patch also allows new inheritance states that pg_dump has to reproduce.

objections.title: F492 marked complete while ALTER CONSTRAINT ENFORCED is rejected for not-null
objections.failure_scenario: A user reads sql_features.txt, sees F492 listed as YES with no remark, and writes `alter table t alter constraint t_x_not_null enforced` for a not-null constraint, as they would for a foreign key. The server raises an error. The user learns from the error that support covers only part of the syntax the conformance table now claims.
objections.argument: The patch removes the "except not-null constraints" remark, but the v6 commit message (message #17) says ALTER CONSTRAINT ... [NOT] ENFORCED is not supported for not-null constraints. The commit message implies other constraint types accept it, and message #14 cites a separate commit that added enforceability changes elsewhere. So not-null constraints would remain the one type with a partial F492, and only the remark's wording changes. A committer would likely ask for the remark to be rewritten to name the gap rather than dropped.
objections.author_must_show: Does F492 in the standard include changing enforcement through ALTER CONSTRAINT, and if so, why should the remark go away before that works?

critic.reasoning: The v6 commit message both removes the remark and says ALTER CONSTRAINT ... [NOT] ENFORCED is unsupported for not-null constraints. Nothing in the thread says whether F492 covers that syntax, so the question stands and a reworded remark would answer it.

objections.title: No user need shown beyond removing the F492 remark
objections.failure_scenario: A user who wants an informational "never null" marker today can write CHECK (col IS NOT NULL) NOT ENFORCED. With the patch, that user gets a second spelling with the same runtime effect: nulls are accepted, attnotnull stays false and the proposal does not say the planner uses it. Postgres would then carry a new constraint state that adds nothing for this user.
objections.argument: Message #1 and the v6 commit message give one reason: completing F492 in sql_features.txt. No message in the thread names a user, a field report, an ETL or data-warehouse workflow, or a migration from another system that needs this syntax. Reviewers in messages #10, #15 and #16 test the patch and comment on its wording, but none of them asks for the feature. An unenforced CHECK constraint already gives the same documentation-only meaning.
objections.author_must_show: Which users or migration tools need NOT NULL NOT ENFORCED specifically, and why does CHECK (col IS NOT NULL) NOT ENFORCED not serve them?

critic.reasoning: The thread gives standard conformance as the only reason and shows no user or tool that needs the syntax. Committer engagement and the existing NOT ENFORCED support for CHECK and foreign keys lower the weight, but they do not show demand.

objections.title: SET NOT NULL errors and gives no route to enforce the constraint
objections.failure_scenario: A schema migration tool runs `alter table t alter column x set not null` on a column that has a NOT ENFORCED not-null constraint. Today SET NOT NULL either adds the constraint or does nothing. With the patch it raises an error, and the only way forward is to drop the constraint and run SET NOT NULL again.
objections.argument: Message #1 and message #17 make SET NOT NULL, VALIDATE CONSTRAINT and ALTER CONSTRAINT ... ENFORCED all fail on a not-enforced not-null constraint, so the state is one-way. Message #4 suggested `SET NOT NULL NOT ENFORCED` and letting SET NOT NULL do the expected thing, and the thread has no answer to it. SET NOT NULL is the usual Postgres verb for not-null, so a NOT ENFORCED form that only ADD CONSTRAINT can create, and that SET NOT NULL cannot turn into an enforced one, departs from existing practice without a stated reason.
objections.author_must_show: Why should SET NOT NULL on a not-enforced not-null constraint raise an error instead of enforcing and validating it, as it does for a column without one?

critic.reasoning: SET NOT NULL validates a NOT VALID not-null constraint today, so an error for the not-enforced case departs from that practice. Message #4 proposed SET NOT NULL forms and no visible reply addresses them.

objections.title: Dump of mixed-enforcement inheritance trees is not shown to round-trip
objections.failure_scenario: A user has a child table that inherits a NOT ENFORCED not-null from one parent and an enforced one from a second parent, so the child gets an enforced constraint. pg_dump decides whether to print the child's not-null from what the parents have, and could leave it out. After restore the child accepts nulls, and nobody sees it until bad rows appear.
objections.argument: [P20] was reverted because pg_dump could not dump every structure the patch allowed, and this patch adds new mixed states to the same inheritance logic. Message #11 shows that flagInhAttrs() decides what to print for inherited not-nulls and was written before enforcement could differ between parent and child. Message #13 reports 002_pg_dump.pl failing for v4, and message #16 tested v5 dumps only in general terms. No message lists the parent and child combinations that were dumped and restored.
objections.author_must_show: For each allowed parent and child combination, including conflicting multiple parents and partitions, does a dump and restore give the same conenforced and attnotnull on every table?

precedents.title: Revert "Improve compression and storage support with inheritance"

critic.reasoning: Message #16 reports pg_dump testing only in general terms, and no reply confirms that v6 fixed the 002_pg_dump.pl failures from message #13. The reason recorded for [P20], pg_dump unable to dump every allowed structure, is the same kind of risk.

objections.title: Every future not-null change pays for a state few will use
objections.failure_scenario: A later patch changes not-null handling in inheritance, partition attach, MERGE/SPLIT PARTITIONS or pg_dump. It must also handle the not-enforced case and its parent/child rules. If it misses that case, mixed hierarchies dump or attach wrongly, and someone finds out at restore or attach time.
objections.argument: The rules span multiple inheritance, partitions, MERGE/SPLIT PARTITIONS (which v4 broke, message #14), pg_dump flagInhAttrs (message #11) and a changed meaning of attnotnull. The author notes that changing enforceability later would bring the complexity of an earlier commit, which future work must face (message #14). All later not-null work carries this cost, but the gain is limited to users of an unenforced not-null constraint, and the thread shows none. An engaged committer (messages #2, #12) lowers the risk but does not supply the demand.
objections.author_must_show: What use of not-enforced not-null constraints justifies the extra inheritance, partitioning and pg_dump rules that every later not-null patch must keep correct?

critic.reasoning: Message #14 reports that v4 failed for MERGE/SPLIT PARTITIONS, which shows that not-null code paths must each learn the new state. The thread shows a committer engaged but no user who gains from that cost.

refuted.title: attnotnull no longer tells whether a not-null constraint exists
refuted.failure_scenario: A later core patch, an extension or a schema tool uses attnotnull to find or rule out a not-null constraint on a column. With this patch the column can have a pg_constraint row while attnotnull is false. Duplicate-constraint checks, DROP NOT NULL or dump logic built on attnotnull then misbehave, and nothing reports it until a user hits the case.
refuted.argument: In message #2 Álvaro Herrera recalls that attnotnull was meant to show that a constraint exists, whatever its validity. Message #6 accepts a different rule only partly, and the v6 catalogs.sgml hunk narrows the meaning to "enforced". Most callers have read attnotnull as a shortcut for "a not-null constraint row exists". The proposal does not list the callers it changed, and nothing makes a future caller that relies on the old meaning fail loudly.
refuted.author_must_show: Which core places read attnotnull to mean a not-null constraint exists, how did each change, and what makes a future caller choose the right test?

critic.reasoning: Message #2 raised this point, message #5 answered it, and in message #6 the committer agreed that attnotnull exists to tell applications a null insert will fail. That meaning is kept, and the scenario names no caller that breaks.

refuted.title: The hard part, changing enforceability, is deferred
refuted.failure_scenario: A user creates NOT NULL NOT ENFORCED during a migration and later wants it enforced. ALTER CONSTRAINT ENFORCED, VALIDATE CONSTRAINT and SET NOT NULL all fail, so the only route is to drop the constraint and add it again. On inherited or partitioned tables, the drop and the re-add each recurse through the hierarchy.
refuted.argument: Message #14 names the complexity of commit 0cd17fdd3c and answers that the patch is safe because enforceability cannot change yet. The patch still fixes the inheritance rules that a later ALTER CONSTRAINT ENFORCED must keep, so the recursive and hardest work falls on a later patch and its committer. Not-null constraints are an area where earlier catalog work was reverted twice for problems found late ([P7], [P1]). This argues for knowing the full design before the syntax is fixed.
refuted.author_must_show: What design would ALTER CONSTRAINT ... ENFORCED use for not-null constraints across inheritance and partitions, and do the v6 rules permit it without change?

precedents.title: Revert "Catalog NOT NULL constraints" and fallout
Revert structural changes to not-null constraints

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of standards-compat-2 for the user-facing scenario. [P7] and [P1] record pg_upgrade and late structural problems, which say nothing about enforceability, and CHECK constraints also gained NOT ENFORCED before ALTER CONSTRAINT could change it.

refuted.title: Only standard conformance is offered against new inheritance complexity
refuted.failure_scenario: Every later change to not-null handling in inheritance, partitioning, MERGE/SPLIT PARTITIONS, LIKE or pg_dump must now cover a third state. If a change misses it, a not-enforced child sits under an enforced parent or the dump does not restore. The patch says nulls are accepted, so the user gets no protection in return.
refuted.argument: Message #1 and the commit message cite only removing the F492 remark. The thread shows no user report or workload. A not-enforced CHECK can at least describe an expression, but a not-enforced not-null constraint carries one bit, and the thread does not say whether the planner uses that bit. Ten conformance-only patches of this size, about 89 KB, would be hard to keep in step. Álvaro Herrera's engagement as committer lowers the ownership risk but does not supply demand.
refuted.author_must_show: Which users or tools need a not-null constraint that does not reject nulls, and what do they do today without it?

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of demand-2, which states the same cost against the same missing demand with more specific thread references.

refuted.title: CHECK (col IS NOT NULL) NOT ENFORCED already gives the same behavior
refuted.failure_scenario: A user who wants an informational not-null declaration can already write `check (x is not null) not enforced`, which stores the intent and accepts nulls. The patch adds a second way to say this, with its own inheritance, partitioning and pg_dump rules. Every later change to not-null handling, such as supporting ALTER CONSTRAINT ... ENFORCED, must also keep these rules correct.
refuted.argument: With attnotnull left false and no use by the planner or executor, a NOT ENFORCED not-null constraint behaves like the NOT ENFORCED CHECK form Postgres already accepts. Its only extra is the standard syntax and the removal of the F492 remark (message #1, message #17), and no user request is shown. Message #14 says the complexity of commit 0cd17fdd3c is avoided only because enforceability cannot be changed yet. That cost comes back if it ever can, in a catalog area that has been reverted twice.
refuted.author_must_show: What can a user, tool or the planner do with NOT NULL NOT ENFORCED that `check (col is not null) not enforced` cannot do today?

precedents.title: Revert structural changes to not-null constraints
Revert "Catalog NOT NULL constraints" and fallout

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of demand-1, which makes the same CHECK (col IS NOT NULL) NOT ENFORCED point. [P1] and [P7] concern cataloging not-null constraints and must not be used as support.

touch_points.label: catalog changes
touch_points.reason: pg_attribute.attnotnull now means an enforced not-null constraint exists; pg_constraint rows for not-null can have conenforced false.

touch_points.label: ABI / extension API
touch_points.reason: The patch touches tupdesc.h, heap.h and pg_constraint.h, which extensions include.

touch_points.label: SQL-standard conflict or non-standard syntax
touch_points.reason: The patch adds NOT NULL NOT ENFORCED syntax in gram.y and removes the F492 remark in sql_features.txt.

touch_points.label: planner behaviour change
touch_points.reason: relcache.c and tupdesc.h change how column nullability is computed; the thread does not say whether the planner uses a not-enforced constraint.

touch_points.label: pg_dump / restore round-trip
touch_points.reason: pg_dump.c emits NOT NULL NOT ENFORCED inline, and 002_pg_dump.pl failed for v4.

touch_points.label: psql UX conventions
touch_points.reason: describe.c changes \d output, and the tab completion question has no visible answer.

touch_points.label: maintenance burden ("who maintains this in 10 years")
touch_points.reason: Inheritance, partitioning, MERGE/SPLIT PARTITIONS, LIKE and pg_dump code must each handle a not-enforced not-null state.

touch_points.label: doesn't fit what Postgres is about (extension / external tool / already solved)
touch_points.reason: CHECK (col IS NOT NULL) NOT ENFORCED already gives the same runtime behavior.

questions: Does F492 in the standard include changing enforcement through ALTER CONSTRAINT, and if so, should the sql_features.txt remark name that gap instead of being removed?
Why should SET NOT NULL on a column with a not-enforced not-null constraint raise an error instead of enforcing and validating the constraint?
For each allowed parent and child combination, including conflicting multiple parents and partitions, does dump and restore give the same conenforced and attnotnull on every table?
Does the planner or executor ever use a not-enforced not-null constraint, for example to prove IS NOT NULL?
Which users or migration tools need NOT NULL NOT ENFORCED, and why does CHECK (col IS NOT NULL) NOT ENFORCED not serve them?

committability.owner_note: Álvaro Herrera is the listed committer and reviewed the design in message #2; the work needs someone who knows not-null constraint inheritance and pg_dump.
committability.liability: The owner signs for the new attnotnull meaning and for a not-enforced state in inheritance, partitioning and pg_dump, with no end date.
committability.author_follow_up: The author posted six versions over 14 months, followed the committer's review, and moved the entry forward across CommitFests.

priority.reason: The thread gives only standard conformance as the reason, so the audience is small. The patch is about 89 KB across tablecmds.c, the catalog code and pg_dump, but a qualified committer is engaged and the open points are fixable.

provisional_note: Without the code, this review could not check whether information_schema views and other readers of not-null pg_constraint rows test conenforced, or whether v6 fixed the 002_pg_dump.pl failures reported for v4.
disclosure: Prepared by an AI harness; treat as a devil's advocate, not a verdict.

precedents_retrieved.title: Fix pg_get_constraintdef for NOT NULL constraints on domains
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Fix pg_get_constraintdef for NOT NULL constraints on domains
Reverted commit(s): Revert structural changes to not-null constraints
precedents_retrieved.objection:
We added pg_constraint rows for all not-null constraints, first for
tables and later for domains; but while the ones for tables were
reverted, the ones for domains were not.  However, we did accidentally
revert ruleutils.c support for the ones on domains in 6f8bb7c1e961,
which breaks running pg_get_constraintdef() on them.  Put that back.

This is only needed in branch 17, because we've reinstated this code in
branch master with commit 14e87ffa5c54.  Add some new tests in both
branches.

I couldn't find anything else that needs de-reverting.

precedents_retrieved.title: Change a constraint's index - ALTER TABLE ... ALTER CONSTRAINT ... USING INDEX ...
precedents_retrieved.objectors: Tom Lane, Alvaro Herrera, Laurenz Albe
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds ALTER TABLE ... ALTER CONSTRAINT ... USING INDEX to replace the index behind an EXCLUDE, UNIQUE, PRIMARY KEY or FOREIGN KEY constraint with a similar index. The main use case is swapping a primary key index for one with INCLUDE columns, or back.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Tom Lane wanted the feature rejected because a primary key with a swapped index is no longer an accurate primary key, and information_schema cannot describe it. Alvaro Herrera and Laurenz Albe agreed that primary keys with INCLUDE columns would first need PRIMARY KEY syntax, so that pg_dump works. That leaves this command a narrow use case. The author did not answer the review, and Michael Paquier marked the entry returned with feedback.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
TBH I think if we really wanted the feature of primary keys with
included columns, we'd have to add it to the PRIMARY KEY syntax rather
than having an ad-hoc ALTER TABLE ALTER CONSTRAINT USING INDEX command
to replace the index underneath.

precedents_retrieved.title: Fix warnings under ENFORCE_REGRESSION_TEST_NAME_RESTRICTIONS
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch renamed roles and databases in the SSL TAP tests to use the regress_ and regression_ prefixes, and regenerated the certificates to match. This removed the backend warnings that the SSL tests produce when Postgres is built with ENFORCE_REGRESSION_TEST_NAME_RESTRICTIONS.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The naming rule exists to protect clusters with useful data during "make installcheck", and TAP tests always run on one-off clusters, so they have nothing to protect. Extending the rule to TAP tests would need the WARNING raised to an ERROR to find all violations, and fixing a single TAP suite was judged not worth doing. About 400 similar warnings remained after the patch.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
TAP tests always use one-off test clusters, so there is no hazard
to guard against.

precedents_retrieved.title: Add ALWAYS DEFERRED option for CONSTRAINTs and CONSTRAINT TRIGGERs
precedents_retrieved.summary: Add ALWAYS DEFERRED option for CONSTRAINTs and CONSTRAINT TRIGGERs

precedents_retrieved.title: Enforce creation of destination folders for source files in pg_regress
precedents_retrieved.objectors: Robert Haas, Stephen Frost, Peter Eisentraut
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch makes pg_regress create the sql/ and expected/ output directories when a test suite uses only source files and those directories are missing. Extensions would then no longer need to keep empty sql/ and expected/ directories that hold only a .gitignore ignoring everything.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Reviewers saw no clear gain, because .gitignore entries for the generated files are still needed, and keeping them inside the existing directories is better than moving them one level up. Robert Haas asked what is wrong with a .gitignore that ignores everything, and Stephen Frost recommended rejection after his review. The author then noted that three committers were unconvinced and nobody else supported the patch, and agreed to mark it rejected.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: I don't see this as an improvement. What's wrong with a .gitignore file ignoring everything?

precedents_retrieved.title: Revert "Catalog NOT NULL constraints" and fallout
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Revert "Catalog NOT NULL constraints" and fallout
Reverted commit(s): Catalog NOT NULL constraints
precedents_retrieved.objection:
This reverts commit e056c557aef4 and minor later fixes thereof.

There's a few problems in this new feature -- most notably regarding
pg_upgrade behavior, but others as well.  This new feature is not in any
way critical on its own, so instead of scrambling to fix it we revert it
and try again in early 17 with these issues in mind.

precedents_retrieved.title: CHECK constraint deferrable Support
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch lets CHECK constraints be declared DEFERRABLE, as the SQL standard allows, so they can be checked at commit time and controlled with SET CONSTRAINTS. The author's use case was a CHECK that calls a function counting rows in another table, deferred until related rows exist.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The visible messages do not say why the entry was withdrawn, and the author posts nothing after the v3 patch. Tom Lane objected that the CHECK implementation assumes immutable conditions, so a deferrable CHECK built on it adds little and invites misuse. David G. Johnston argued that making NOT NULL deferrable would cover the real use cases. Dean Rasheed reported open bugs, among them wrong results from constraint exclusion while a deferred constraint is violated.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
I continue to assert that basing this feature on the current
CHECK implementation will produce nothing but a toy feature,
that's not only of little practical use but will be an active
foot-gun for people who expect it to do more than it can.

precedents_retrieved.title: Enforce typmod for function inputs, function results and parameters for spi_prepare'd statements called from PLs
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Enforce typmod for function inputs, function results and parameters for spi_prepare'd statements called from PLs
Section: Functions
Linked: Re: BUG #2917: spi_prepare doesn't accept typename aliases; RFC for adding typmods to functions

precedents_retrieved.title: Revert "pg_dump: Lock all relations, not just plain tables".
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Revert "pg_dump: Lock all relations, not just plain tables".
Reverted commit(s): pg_dump: Lock all relations, not just plain tables; Avoid null pointer dereference if error result lacks SQLSTATE.
precedents_retrieved.objection:
Revert 403a3d91c, as well as the followup fix 7f4235032, in all
branches.  We need to think a bit harder about what the behavior
of LOCK TABLE on views should be, and there's no time for that
before next week's releases.  We'll take another crack at this

precedents_retrieved.title: pg_dump: optimize dumpFunc()
precedents_retrieved.summary: Replace pg_dump's per-function query in dumpFunc() with a single query that gathers data for all functions up front, keeping the PGresult in memory and using a sorted array of function OIDs to locate each function's row. The aim was to reduce dump time for databases with many functions (shown as about 0.25s to about 0.11s for 10k simple functions).
precedents_retrieved.objection: Tom Lane questioned whether the change helps databases with few functions and what it does to pg_dump's memory requirements when there are very many functions with large source text, and said the shown results did not justify the risk. The author agreed and withdrew the patch.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
I'm not sure that the results you're showing justify taking any
risk here.

precedents_retrieved.title: Dump-restore loosing 'attnotnull' bit for DEFERRABLE PRIMARY KEY column(s)
precedents_retrieved.summary: A bug report: after dump and restore, a column covered only by a DEFERRABLE PRIMARY KEY loses attnotnull, because pg_dump emits a throwaway NOT NULL constraint and then drops it. The author's patch changes pg_dump to skip the throwaway NOT NULL constraint for deferrable primary keys.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The visible messages do not show why. Before the patch was posted, Alvaro Herrera said the more critical fix was in the backend, which should reject the DROP CONSTRAINT, and that ATExecDropNotNull() should stop relying on RelationGetIndexAttrBitmap. No message after the patch shows a review or a decision.

precedents_retrieved.title: avoid bitmapOR-ing indexes for scan conditions implied by partition constraint
precedents_retrieved.authors: Justin Pryzby (justinpryzby), Soumyadeep Chakraborty (soumyadeep2007), Soumyadeep Chakraborty (soumyadeepc)
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch makes the planner skip bitmap index scans for arms of an OR clause that the partition constraint refutes, so each partition scans only the useful arms. The change lives in generate_bitmap_or_paths() in indxpath.c and targets queries with long OR lists over many partitions.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Tom Lane objected to fixing this in indxpath.c. The fix helps only bitmap scans, may repeat the same proof, cannot be turned off, leaves row estimates unchanged, and may break the loop that requires each OR arm to match an index. He proposed removing proven quals from baserestrictinfo instead, but measured about 2.5% slowdown on pgbench -S and left the direction open. The entry then sat in Waiting on Author for weeks, and Masahiko Sawada returned it with feedback.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
I really quite dislike solving
this via a kluge in indxpath.c.

precedents_retrieved.title: Improve pg_dump dumping publication tables
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch changes pg_dump's getPublicationTables() to fetch all publication-table memberships with a single query, instead of iterating over every table and issuing a separate query per table. The matching TableInfo for each row is then looked up in tblinfoindex, which should be faster when there are many tables.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The patch was superseded, not rejected: Tom Lane had already committed practically the same change in passing (commit 8e396a773), which also removed the server-side join. He therefore marked the entry withdrawn. Cary Huang's earlier concern about client-side memory use with very many publication tables was answered by Tom Lane as not significant compared to the per-table data pg_dump already collects.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
I'll mark this CF entry "withdrawn", since it wasn't rejected
exactly.  Too bad we don't have a classification of "superseded

roaster_notes.note: No precedent proposes NOT NULL NOT ENFORCED itself. The one objection rests on the pg_dump revert reason in [P20], which applies here and which the thread does not settle.
pg_dump output was settled in messages #9 to #13, and the attnotnull meaning in messages #5 and #6, so neither is raised here.

The proposal adds no WAL records, on-disk format, wire messages or catalog columns. It reuses pg_constraint.conenforced and convalidated, which already exist for CHECK and foreign key constraints, and pg_upgrade only meets clusters that hold no not-enforced not-null constraints. The patch narrows pg_attribute.attnotnull to mean an enforced constraint exists. This breaks the earlier rule that attnotnull is set whenever a not-null constraint row exists, but Herrera agreed in message #6 and v6 documents the change, so the point is settled. Not checked without the code: whether information_schema views and other code reading contype 'n' rows check conenforced.

No privilege or exposure aspect: adding or dropping a not-null constraint already requires table ownership, and NOT ENFORCED only weakens a check the owner controls. Whether the planner or information_schema treats a not-enforced constraint as a guarantee is a correctness question for another angle, and it cannot be checked without the code.
Not applicable. Ownership risk is lower than usual because Álvaro Herrera is the listed committer and reviewed the design in the thread.
One objection from this angle. The only alternative found is the existing NOT ENFORCED CHECK constraint, and it does not provide the standard NOT NULL syntax.
Objections are 'not now, show demand'. The design was reviewed by an engaged committer, so this angle does not claim the design is wrong.
